html:
The Malagasy political crisis began in early 2009, when the young mayor of Antananarivo, Andry Rajoelina, led protests against President Marc Ravalomanana, who was forced out in March with the backing of the army.

Ravalomanana, a dairy businessman, had won power in the disputed election of 2001 against Ratsiraka. Rajoelina accused him of autocracy and of a plan to lease vast farm lands to a Korean company. Security forces killed protesters marching on the palace.

The African Union and donors suspended Madagascar and cut aid, and the economy suffered. Elections only in 2013 restored a recognised government. Rajoelina was later elected president himself, and was in turn removed by the military in 2025 after youth protests, showing how often power in the capital changes hands by force.
sum: The Malagasy political crisis began in early 2009, when the young mayor of Antananarivo, Andry Rajoelina, led protests against President Marc Ravalomanana, who was forced out in March with the backing of the army.
